correctness.rationale: Each local depolarizer acts diagonally on the four matrix units; the output has only a single corner coherence and symmetric complementary computational populations. For each nontrivial cut the partial transpose has exactly one candidate negative 2x2 block. Its equal diagonal entries are P*cosh((r L(s)-L(d))/2); the offdiagonal is s^(n-1)d/2, so its negative eigenvalue proves the formula including the zero boundary. Strict monotonicity of cosh on the nonnegative axis gives the unique/two-tie parity-nearest-lattice cut classes, exact switch conditions and binomial multiplicities. The published Dür--Cirac theorem applies because every noncorner GHZ eigenpair has equal weights. At s*=1/sqrt(5), g(s*)=0 and g'(s*)=5sqrt(5)/4; fixed defect visibility bounds the optimizing lattice index, yielding the normalized limit and strict-regime classification. A genuine derivative jump at each resonance follows from distance-to-lattice cusp times nonzero sinh. The standalone verifier constructs 20 density matrices directly, checks 228 partial transposes, 12 near-critical sequences and four tie surfaces. No conclusion is claimed at the critical equality or for full multipartite distillability.

originality.rationale: The exact local-output formula and all-cut nearest-parity-lattice optimization are absent from the six materially compared primary sources. The strongest 1999 and 2021 sources cover the general GHZ-diagonal PPT machinery, while the 2001/2008 sources cover symmetric local channels. The assessed contribution is the explicit one-defect maximizer, resonance multiplicities and sharp parity-dependent finite-size critical law, not the known PPT criterion or bulk homogeneous threshold. Equivalent unpublished or unindexed specializations remain possible; the outcome is not an independent priority certification.

value.rationale: Entanglement survival and the most entangled bipartitions under one unequal local noise parameter are natural finite-size quantities in quantum memories with a site-specific fault or high-quality qubit. The previously universal balanced-cut maximizer can move through a complete parity-resonant sequence of unbalanced cuts as the defect improves. The exact class multiplicities and infinite family of sharp order-1/n critical-offset kinks quantify a structural, experimentally motivated nonuniform-noise effect. This is an exact all-dimensional parameter classification rather than a textbook reformulation of a particular homogeneous bound; its scope is expressly limited to one defect.
